items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I had never heard of her before, but she had a fine voice.

ctx.x: During the six weeks we rehearsed we had to take a health examination which Ben Smith did not pass. Therefore, Herbie had to replace Ben and I felt sad about it because we had been together in Andy Kirk's orchestra and besides being a fine musician, he was a great person whom I had plenty of fun with. "Kat" engaged an alto player named Curby Alexander. We had to be inoculated against smallpox, Typhoid-paratyphoid, tetnus, typhus, cholera, yellow fever, and on the physical examination card in miscellaneous, it is…

Willie Bryant, the exband leader and show man, was the Master of Ceremonies for our group, whose unit number was 789. The girl singer engaged was named Melrose Colbert and whom I found out later was Ray Nance, the Ellington trumpet and violin virtuoso's first wife. She was now his ex-wife. I had never heard of her before, but she had a fine voice. The comedy act was Henry Matthews, known as Shorty and Alfred Chester, known as Slick. He was the straight man and Shorty was the comical one in the act. There was also…

The last two weeks of the rehearsals, I worked two nights a week at the 3 Deuces and 52nd Street with George Johnson who replaced the two bands actually playing there on their nights off, which one had on Monday and the other Tuesday. Monday was always the day that I was inoculated, and my arm would give me hell Monday and Tuesday nights. And not being allowed to drink alcohol because of the shots didn't give me much inspiration to play, but at least I tried. The second and last week, one night I blacked out for…
